newsitem.title: USA: Gaming sector disappoints in US high-yield market.
newsitem.headline: Gaming sector disappoints in US high-yield market.

text.p: Poor earnings reports depressed prices for the debt of a pair of junk-rated gaming concerns in otherwise quiet high-yield trade on Friday, dealers said.
Prices there were otherwise mostly unchanged in the face of waning U.S. Treasuries, dealers said, with recent new issues trading at or above Thursday's closing levels.

Casino America Inc debt was one of the day's casualties following the company's announcement it expects to report a $3.5 to $5 million loss for the quarter ending October 31. The loss does not include an extraordinary tax charge of $12.2 million incurred by a debt refinancing.
Casino America's 12-1/2s of 2003 eroded four points to a 96-1/2 bid, 98-1/2 offer market in light trade, a trader said.

Argosy Gaming Co blamed increased competitive pressures in Iowa, Kansas City and St. Louis for a third-quarter loss of $0.32 per share vs a $0.07 profit a year earlier. The debt dropped about two points from Thursday to 93-3/4 bid, 94-3/4 offer in early trade. It had traded as high as 98-1/2 bid, 99-1/2 offer on Wednesday following the rejection of an Ohio gaming referendum.
Argosy Gaming is developing an Indiana-based riverboat casino just outside Cincinnati, Ohio.
Computer products distributor Merisel Inc debt fell to 52-1/2 bid, 55 offer after reporting a $117 million Q3 loss, a high-yield trader said.
New high-yield issues enjoyed firm markets.
--Stuart Entertainment Inc's $100 million 12.5 percent senior subordinate notes due 2004 traded near par on Friday after fading to 99-5/8 in aftermarket trade on Thursday.
--Amtrol's $115 million 10-5/8s 10-year debt saw a 100-1/2, 101-1/4 market after a par pricing on Thursday.
--Blue Chip Casino's $86 million 13-3/4s of 2003 were quoted at 103 bid following a par pricing on Thursday.

Turning to investment grades, spreads were flat as prices eased with U.S. Treasuries, dealers said. Governments fell after the Commerce Department said wholesale inventories fell 1.3 percent in September, leading some analysts to forecast a fourth quarter economic rebound.
The White House quickly dispelled a rumor that President Bill Clinton was shot, which had prompted some government market instability.
Two large new issues were priced.

--BellSouth Capital Funding issued $300 million 30-year AA1/AAA rated debentures at par to yield 6.04 percent via a Morgan Stanley & Co Inc syndicate. The debentures were priced with five and 10-year puts.
--Anheuser Busch issued $250 million 10-year A1/AA-minus rated debentures as 6-3/4s to yield 6.824 percent or 55 basis points over the Treasury curve via Dillon Read & Co Inc.
Standard & Poor's move on Thursday to revised its rating outlook on Anheuser Busch to negative from stable will not affect the deal, one trader said.
"What's the downside, single-A?," the trader said.
